sources.entry: BuddyPress - Powerful plugin that takes your WordPress.org powered site beyond the blog with social-network features like user profiles, activity streams, user groups, and more. (Source Code) GPL-2.0 PHP

summary.one_liner: BuddyPress is a WordPress plugin that adds social-network features such as user profiles, activity streams, and user groups to a WordPress site.
summary.what_it_does: BuddyPress is a WordPress plugin that turns a WordPress site into a community site with social-network features like user profiles, activity streams, and user groups. The repository is a mirror of the project's development SVN repository, and the README asks contributors to submit patches to SVN rather than pull requests here. The README covers only the local development setup: it uses Node/npm and Docker with the wp-env tool to start, stop, and restart a local WordPress environment, and it describes how to log in and generate an admin password. It does not describe end-user features in detail beyond the listing description. The project is PHP, MySQL, and JavaScript based.
use_cases: build a community or social network on WordPress
add user profiles to a WordPress site
create user groups on a WordPress site
add activity streams to a WordPress site
set up a local BuddyPress development environment
how_to_run: Install Node and npm (for example: brew install node, choco install node, or apt install nodejs npm)
Install Docker and make sure it is running
npm run wp-env stop (to stop the environment)
notable: Mirror of the official SVN development repository; pull requests are not accepted here
Ships a local development environment started with a single npm command using Docker
Adds social-network features to an existing WordPress site rather than being standalone software
Listed on awesome-selfhosted under social networks and forums
caveats: Requires WordPress; it is a plugin, not a standalone application
Pull requests are not accepted in this mirror; patches go to the SVN repository
README covers only the development environment, not end-user installation or features
